speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling and easy bruising on your mother's side, I suspect a clotting factor deficiency. REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Factor VIII and IX levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time (PT): 15 sec, Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT): 60 sec. Factor VIII and IX levels were not measured in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT suggests a defect in the intrinsic pathway, likely involving Factor VIII or IX. Do you recall if your uncle was specifically diagnosed with Hemophilia A or B, and have you ever experienced bleeding into your joints after minor injuries? REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII activity level, Factor IX activity level, Von Willebrand Factor antigen and activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is unusual for Factor VIII and IX to be normal if the PTT is prolonged by those factors, so we must look for other causes like an inhibitor or Von Willebrand disease. Given the family history and easy bruising, I need to rule out Von Willebrand Disease more thoroughly. REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor antigen, Von Willebrand Factor activity, and Ristocetin cofactor activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Von Willebrand Disease and common hemophilias are ruled out, I suspect a rarer factor deficiency or an inhibitor. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI, XII, and VII levels, plus a mixing study.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VII is normal, the normal PT rules out common extrinsic pathway defects, but the prolonged PTT with normal Factor VIII, IX, and XI suggests a rarer deficiency or a lupus anticoagulant. REQUEST TEST: Factor X, Factor V, and Factor II levels, along with a Bethesda assay for inhibitors.

speaker: Doctor
text: With all standard clotting factors and inhibitors ruling out, the prolonged PTT is likely due to a contact activation factor deficiency like Factor XII, which causes bleeding diathesis in some cases despite being asymptomatic in others. REQUEST TEST: Factor XII level, Factor XI level, and a repeat PTT with a mixing study to confirm correction.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since all clotting factors are normal and the PTT remains prolonged, this likely represents a laboratory artifact due to the presence of a lupus anticoagulant, which can prolong PTT in vitro without causing clinical bleeding. REQUEST IMAGES: Coagulation profile summary and patient clinical notes. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lupus Anticoagulant
